subject: general
question: Which countries began assuming responsibilities as non-permanent members of the United Nations Security Council for two-year term?

options.text: Denmark, Japan, Pakistan, Greece, and Somalia
Japan, Germany, India, Greece, and Panama
Denmark, Pakistan, Greece, India, and Panama
Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia

solution:
The correct answer is ​**Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] __In News__**

__
 
• Denmark, Greece, Pakistan, Panama, and Somalia have assumed roles as **non-permanent members** of the UN Security Council, starting their **two-year term on January 1, 2025**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Replaced Countries**: The five countries replaced Ecuador, Japan, Malta, Mozambique, and Switzerland.
 
• **Ceremony**: A **flag installation ceremony** was held at the UN headquarters in New York, initiated by Kazakhstan in 2018.
 
• **Remarks**:
 
 
• Kazakh UN Ambassador Kairat Umarov congratulated the new members.
 
• Algerian UN Ambassador Amar Bendjama, as the **Security Council President for January**, emphasized the responsibility of upholding multilateralism.
 
 
 
• **Council Composition**:
 
 
• 15 members total: 5 **permanent members** (Britain, China, France, Russia, US) and 10 **non-permanent members** elected for two-year terms.
 
• Five non-permanent members are replaced annually.
 
 

The new members are tasked with addressing global challenges and contributing to international peace and security during their tenure.
